subject: Request: references for HIPAA-compliant inference (healthcare)
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: James Porter <james.porter@hearthstonehealth.com>, Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@hearthstonehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 05 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: references for HIPAA-compliant inference (healthcare)

Hi James / Olivia —

Thanks again for a great conversation yesterday. As we discussed during the deal review, the procurement team has asked to speak with a couple of existing customers who are running healthcare PII/PHI workloads on a private deployment (VPC or on-prem) and can speak to latency, reliability, and controls around data residency and auditing.

To make the reference calls helpful, could you tell us which of the following matters most to your stakeholders?
- Deployment model: Private VPC vs Dedicated vs On‑prem
- Throughput profile: bursty spikes vs sustained RPS (please share approx target RPS)
- Observability / logs: level of token-level tracing and audit retention needed
- Security artifacts: SOC 2 + HIPAA attestation vs signed BAAs

If you prefer, we can curate 2–3 brief 20–30 minute calls matched to your priorities (region: US West preferred). We can limit reference calls to technical leads and procurement if that helps speed things up.

Attached a short one‑pager that summarizes customers in healthcare that are okay with reference calls and what they typically cover. Proposed window: this week or early next week — what works for you?

Thanks — I’ll loop in Monica and Tessa from our customer success team to coordinate scheduling and any documentation you need.

Best,
Rishi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: reference-onepager.pdf (1 page)]

From: James Porter <james.porter@hearthstonehealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Apr 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: references for HIPAA-compliant inference (healthcare)

Rishi —

Appreciate the follow-up. Two quick clarifications from our side before we schedule calls:
1) We need references that are running in a private VPC or on‑prem (not hosted multi-tenant).
2) Prefer customers in the US West region and those that operate with ~150–300 RPS sustained during batch windows.
3) We want a ~30-minute technical call with their ML/Platform lead and a 10–15 minute procurement chat if they can accommodate it.

We can do calls this Thursday or Friday afternoon (PST). Also, procurement will want confirmation that a BAA is in place or that the customer is willing to speak under a standard non‑disclosure for the call.

If you can share 2–3 options (name, title, 15‑second match summary) and an indication if they’ve signed a BAA or a consent form, we’ll pick and lock slots.

Thanks,
James Porter
Sr. Director, Product & Clinical Ops
Hearthstone Health

Suggested matches from our reference pool (short notes):
1) MedAxis Health — Contact: Sara Lowe, Head of Platform (sara.lowe@medaxishealth.com). Running Redwood Private (VPC) in us-west, production inference for triage models (~200 RPS sustained during batch windows). Signed consent (we have their permission historically for references).
2) CrestView Clinics — Contact: Malik Reyes, CTO (malik.reyes@crestviewclinic.com). Dedicated pool, good telemetry on p95s and replay traces; can speak to fallback/routing policies.
3) Arbor Diagnostics — Contact: Priya Rao, VP Engineering (priya.rao@arbordx.com). On‑prem deployment, strict data residency and audit logs; can speak to BAA and audit artifacts.

Attachments: customer-reference-briefs.pdf (contains one‑pager summaries and suggested call topics). I’ve flagged MedAxis as the closest match for throughput & VPC in us-west. Monica / Tessa — can you confirm:
- Whether MedAxis will accept a 30‑minute technical call + 15‑minute procurement?
- If we need a signed consent / BAA for the call, and if you have the most recent consent PDF (attach if available).

If green, I’ll propose two time slots on Thu/ Fri PST for Hearthstone and ask them to pick.

Thanks — Rishi
